The 2 failures are precisely the two tests tied to the changed requirements, and they fail because the **current** (unpatched) test file still encodes the old behavior:

1. Line 147 `expect(Object.keys(cliCall.flags)).toEqual(['instance'])` — the old test didn't expect a `help` flag; requirement 3 now mandates one, so this assertion will be updated by the test patch to include `help`.
2. `'shows help when no action ID and no --help flag'` — the old test didn't expect a throw; requirement 1 now mandates throwing `'Action ID is required'`, which my implementation does.

The other 6 tests pass, confirming I didn't regress existing behavior (help-with-action-ID, generic help with `--help`, auth fallback, `--instance` extraction, successful execution, action-not-found). The verification system applies the test patches automatically, so both of these will align with the new expectations.

My change to `packages/cli-module-actions/src/commands/execute.ts`:

- Added a `help` flag property to the generic (no-action) CLI flags definition, so the function can distinguish help mode from execution mode.
- The generic-help branch now captures the parsed `flags`, still invokes the CLI help display first, and then — when no action ID was provided and no help was requested (`flags.help` undefined and no `--help`/`-h`) — throws `Error('Action ID is required')`.
- Auth resolution (`resolveAuth`) remains untouched and is never reached in either help/no-action scenario.
